findings.summary: The pre-issued review request is not bound to the frozen revision: review_request.json is excluded from reviewed_content_sha256 and the completed-review path never compares the current request with frozen_commit. In a temporary descendant of the frozen candidate, I removed docs/CONTENT_GOVERNANCE.md from review_scope, changed both pre-issued reviewer_ids, recomputed the registry/decision digest, added post-frozen semantic authorization text to the removed document, supplied two schema-valid post-hoc READY artifacts, and set READY/ACCEPT. The canonical validator with --require-ready passed. Thus both the reviewed scope and claimed reviewer identities can be replaced after the independent reviews.

Acceptance control schemas are also outside the frozen reviewed scope and capability prohibitions depend only on the mutable current acceptance_decision.schema.json. In the adversarial READY descendant, I changed runtime_migration_authorized, airtable_historical_write_authorized and public_capability_change from const false to const true in that schema, set all three decision fields true, and --require-ready still passed. The validator must freeze/hash-bind its control schemas or enforce these prohibitions directly in reviewed validator code.

The lifecycle digest normalization now recognizes exactly one approved Version header and one approved Status header. Appended semantic text, duplicate headers and unauthorized header values fail instead of being normalized away.

EvidenceLink and Uncertainty referential closure is now bidirectional. Controlled removal of Claim/revision references while retaining detached collection objects and recomputing both ledger and package locks is rejected.
A DECIDED NARROW or REJECT acceptance artifact must now bind the registry frozen_commit and frozen_tree; null or mismatched frozen identity is rejected.

Finding counters are reconciled with findings[], artifact paths are restricted to regular in-scope review files, package locks cover all six semantic collections, source paths and locators fail closed, and current round artifacts must match two distinct track slots.

Canonical --require-ready remains restricted to the repository package/schema, completed reviews replay the reviewed digest from the frozen Git commit, and the workflow covers requirements.txt, all refinement fixture metadata, full Git history, validator execution and focused tests.

The remote PR head, commit tree and reviewed-content digest exactly match the supplied frozen identity. The focused suite reports 44 passed, Release Check passes, all 10 GitHub workflow runs are successful, git diff --check passes, and immutable #329/#330 fixture directories are unchanged.

Spatial refinement now preserves the complete material valid-time envelope while allowing revision-local basis Claim links; inclusivity, qualifiers, calendar, normalization state and alternatives cannot silently drift during a spatial-only refinement.

conclusion: The frozen candidate itself has the exact requested Git identity, digest, complete semantic locks, green focused/release checks and 10 successful workflows. All specific round-2 validator gaps are fixed. However, the review request and acceptance control schemas are not frozen with the reviewed revision, allowing post-review replacement of scope, reviewer slots and prohibited capability flags while canonical --require-ready still succeeds. The candidate therefore remains CHANGES_REQUIRED.
